scope: Verify and minimally fix the three review findings about authenticated request binding, persisted content hashes, and YAML key order.

findings.problem: Restoring an old authenticated response or cancellation after reusing its request number closed a new authenticated acceptance request.
findings.fix: Authenticate the closure only when the referenced current request matches the original request in the authenticating event snapshot.
findings.evidence: Three old-source API regressions fail (altered request plus reused response and cancellation). New request stays pending until its assigned human responds.

findings.problem: Removing an empty marked AC or DoD block during serialization made a saved request immediately stale and the response returned HTTP 409.
findings.fix: Hash the shared serializer/parser roundtrip so review entries use the content that the review write persists. Preserve the existing serializer and revision writer.
findings.evidence: Two local Core and two real HTTP regressions fail on the old source. Saved entry hashes now match the task and the assigned read-only human can accept.

findings.problem: Reordering YAML object keys, including nested author/reviewer keys, removed trust from an unchanged completed acceptance.
findings.fix: Use node:util isDeepStrictEqual for order-independent object comparison; array order and values remain significant.
findings.evidence: Old-source API regression produces trustedEntryIds: []; after the fix all three entries stay trusted and the request stays closed.

changes.simplification: Two existing production modules and the shared serializer/parser are reused. No service, store, exported helper, schema, or UI changes were added.

old_source_regressions.note: Each failure reproduced the reported behavior; the key-order assertion was narrowed to semantic review fields because the file revision correctly changes on a reformat.
